name: Carnarvon Gorge
reason: Rule 1/2: Wikivoyage Carnarvon National Park and the Central Queensland Highlands site both name it; sandstone gorge with swim hole, rock art and walks, the headline draw of the park.
objection: The park may itself be the destination with the gorge as its main spot; placement decides that, not inclusion.

name: Carnarvon Gorge Art Gallery
reason: Rule 1/2: the Wikivoyage Carnarvon article mentions the Art Gallery and park pages call its rock art among Australia's finest; a ~10.8 km return walk to a stencil art site.
objection: It is on the Carnarvon Gorge main track, so a placement may fold it into the gorge. Access notices restrict some sites at times.

name: Cathedral Cave
reason: Rule 1/2: park listing says over 1,500 Aboriginal rock art figures in a large overhang reached by the main track; a distinct cultural stop.
objection: Part of the main gorge walk; access can be restricted by park notices.

name: Wards Canyon
reason: Rule 1/2: Wikivoyage Carnarvon article names Wards Canyon among the sights; a narrow mossy side canyon with the only king fern colony in central Queensland.
objection: Short side branch of the gorge track; closures noted on the park site.

name: Boolimba Bluff
reason: Rule 1/2: Wikivoyage Carnarvon names the track to Boolimba Bluff as the easiest to the shelves; the one formed lookout over the gorge mouth.
objection: A lookout on the park's track network; one of many gorge walks.

name: Big Bend
reason: Rule 3: a walkers' camp at the end of the gorge track, not a standalone attraction.
objection: It is the end of the 9.7 km main track, but the camp itself offers nothing separate.

name: Battleship Spur
reason: Rule 1 passes (park page names it, over 1,000 m, views back over the gorge) but it is a steep, remote long walk beyond Boowinda Gorge and one source only.
objection: For: a rewarding lookout for strong walkers. Against: a very long day; part of the gorge walks network.

name: Boowinda Gorge
reason: Park listing: a boulder-lined side canyon beyond Cathedral Cave and part of the Carnarvon Great Walk route; one source and not a short visit from the trailhead.
objection: For: spectacular eroded walls. Against: really a stage of the Great Walk or the route to Battleship Spur, so arguably part of larger spots.

name: Carnarvon Great Walk
reason: Rule 1/2: QPWS names it as a Great Walk (87 km, multi-day, booked ahead); permanent track, a Great Walk is kept even though booked.
objection: It overlaps the gorge's day walks; a booked camping-walk limits spontaneous visits.

name: Blackdown Tableland National Park
reason: Rule 1/2: the Central Queensland Highlands site and RACQ both name it: a sandstone plateau of about 47,950 ha with waterfalls, lookouts and gorge walks (note: the 4WD loop road is closed until 1 Nov 2026 per RACQ, now past).
objection: Whether it is a destination or a single spot depends on its spot count (placement); not a reason to reject.

name: Yaddamen Dhina Lookout
reason: Central Queensland Highlands and RACQ name it: a 200 m, five-minute, wheelchair-accessible walk to a panorama at the car park and picnic area.
objection: For: the main introduction to the park, with picnic tables. Against: a ten-minute stop and an outlook within a park already listed.

name: Gudda Gumoo Gorge
reason: Rule 1/2: RACQ and Central Queensland Highlands both name the gorge track (waterfall over sandstone ledges into a pool, 240 stairs, about 2 hours); the best-known walk in Blackdown Tableland.
objection: The Gudda Gumoo lookout track shares most of the route; folded into this spot.

name: Mook Mook Track
reason: Central Queensland Highlands names it: 2.4 km return across Mimosa Creek to a lookout on the tableland's eastern edge; one source and a short walk.
objection: For: the only east-side lookout. Against: a minor track within a park already listed, one counted source.

name: Goodela Track
reason: Rule 3: a one-hour escarpment track that starts at Yaddamen Dhina Lookout; a section of the park's walks, not a distinct draw.
objection: The track has views of the bluffs, but it is an extension of the lookout area.

name: Mitha Boongulla Lookout
reason: Central Queensland Highlands and RACQ name it: a lookout on the 4WD Loop Road over the plains; suitable only for high-clearance 4WD and the loop was closed for upgrades until 1 November 2026.
objection: For: a named lookout on the park's drive. Against: access limited to 4WD, a short stop on a park track.

name: Lake Maraboon
reason: Rule 1/2: Central Queensland Highlands page: Queensland's second largest lake with fishing, red claw, boating, a lookout and picnic area, 25 km south-west of Emerald; people go for a half-day.
objection: A locals' favourite with limited standalone appeal for visitors from far away.

name: Emerald Big Easel
reason: Rule 3: a quirky roadside icon (giant easel with the van Gogh Sunflowers painting, Morton Park, Emerald); the Central Queensland Highlands site singles out the giant sunflower painting as a photo stop. Counted source opened mentions the painting, not the name 'Big Easel'.
objection: A ten-minute photo stop; the name was not confirmed on the page I opened.

name: Sapphire Gemfields
reason: Rule 1: Central Queensland Highlands and Wikivoyage Central Queensland both name the fossicking area, but it is a region (around Anakie, Rubyvale and Sapphire) rather than one place; destination-layer note.
objection: For: the headline draw of the highlands. Against: a region, not a spot; its specific places (mine tour, fossicking parks, wetland) are the spots.

name: Anakie
reason: Central Queensland Highlands names the town as the gemfields' gateway at the Anakie Crossroads; a town with services and a sculpture rather than a sight of its own.
objection: For: a base for the gemfields. Against: a gateway, covered by the gemfields' own spots.

name: Sapphire Reflections
reason: Central Queensland Highlands names the 12 m glass-panel sculpture at the Anakie Crossroads; a roadside photo stop; one source and a ten-minute visit.
objection: For: a named photo icon. Against: short and one source.

name: Anakie Railway Station
reason: Rule 2: a 1884 heritage station seen from outside (no source describes going in) with a small dam; part of the Anakie town stop.
objection: A heritage stop in a guide's route could qualify, but none was found.

name: The Willows Gemfields
reason: Central Queensland Highlands: a fossicking township and area 35 km south-west of Anakie known for green and yellow sapphires; the draw is its fossicking parks.
objection: For: a separate fossicking area. Against: the fossicking parks, not the township, are the visit; overlaps the gemfields.

name: Glenalva
reason: Rule 3: a designated fossicking area needing a licence, part of the gemfields; no visitor source describes a visit of its own.
objection: Fossicking is the point of the gemfields, but this is one patch of it.

name: Gemfields Wetland Reserve
reason: Rule 1/2: Central Queensland Highlands names it: a 14 ha reserve opened in April 2018 with about 3.6 km of walking and cycling tracks, seating, a restored fossicker's home and viewing areas.
objection: One counted source and a short visit; wetland conditions vary seasonally.

name: Sapphire's Big Ring
reason: Rule 1: only a search summary from Travel Action Matilda, which I could not open; a roadside big-thing photo spot among six on the gemfields.
objection: For: a quirky roadside icon. Against: a five-minute stop with no counted source opened.

name: Miners Heritage Underground Mine Tour
reason: Rule 1/2: Visit Capricorn (opened) says to 'venture underground with a guided mine tour'; the place is a walk-in heritage mine at Rubyvale, a permanent attraction. Rename to the mine (Miners Heritage Walk-In Mine); the tour is how you see it.
objection: An operator-run tour, so the spot should be the place not the tour; the operator's name was not confirmed.
